title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom  on 1968-03-29
lineage: AUD > MR > D > PCM > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Phenomenal 1968 audience tape with crisp Dark Star and a high‑energy four‑song set featuring standout performances of Sittin' On Top, Death Don't Have No Mercy and Good Morning Schoolgirl.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an early‑68 show that sounds astonishingly clear for an audience source – the mix is crisp, the crowd virtually disappears, and the Dark Star is especially mellow and dreamy. Musically the band delivers a loose but kick‑butt performance; four songs flow with high energy, highlighted by a fiery Sittin' On Top Of The World and a blues‑rooted Death Don't Have No Mercy.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both the musical performance (standout songs, high energy) and the surprisingly excellent audience recording quality across >15 detailed reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear sound with minimal crowd noise; superb balance for a 1968 audience tape. Minor flaws are noted but do not detract from overall listenability.

standout_songs: Sittin' On Top Of The World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Four‑song set that feels loose yet tight; a mellow Dark Star opens, followed by an energetic Sittin' On Top, then solid performances of Good Morning Schoolgirl and Death Don't Have No Mercy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for deep‑throated, expressive vocals and strong guitar work, especially on Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Phil: His post‑Sittin' vocal quip is noted; otherwise no specific instrumental comments.
band_member_comments.Keys: Simple keyboard accompaniment mentioned on Death Don't Have No Mercy; adequate for the era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are present, providing solid rhythmic foundation despite occasional single‑drummer feel.
